title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (Q4 2026)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview
========

Short intro: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design, roadmap & themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private). It is intended for product, engineering, solutions, and GTM teams preparing for Q4 2026 commercial launches and Q1 2027 enterprise rollouts.

Goals
-----
- Provide a single coherent product narrative and launch plan for Unified Inference that aligns engineering priorities with go-to-market needs.
- Define measurable requirements and non-functional SLOs for the initial GA release.
- Outline packaging and pricing options that balance unit economics and enterprise procurement needs.
- Document rollout steps, ownership, and rollback criteria.

Non-goals
---------
- This doc does not replace low-level runtime implementation details (see eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture).
- It is not a customer-facing spec or developer SDK reference.

Key features (customer-facing)
-----------------------------
- Unified API: single REST/SDK surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Predictable SLAs: dedicated capacity contracts with 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated customers.
- Cost controls: automated batching, per-route batching profiles, and per-customer quantization recommendations.
- Rollouts & fallbacks: canary and A/B rollout controls with automated fallback to cheaper model variants on capacity pressure.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histogram, and end-to-end tracing integration.

Product requirements (PRD)
-------------------------
Functional requirements:
1. API parity: The Unified API must support the following endpoints and behaviors for GA:
   - /v1/generate (chat/text) with streaming and function/tool calling support.
   - /v1/embeddings returning stable vector shapes (float32) and usage metadata.
   - /v1/rerank accepting candidate lists + configurable scoring options.
2. Model catalog: Maintain model manifests including architecture, quantization profile, tokenization, cost profile, and validated performance benchmarks.
3. Routing policy: Policy engine that routes requests by region, latency SLO, and cost tier with configurable priorities.
4. Access & quotas: Per-API-key rate limiting, per-route quotas, and per-customer reserved capacity ledger for Dedicated.
5. Observability: Per-request tracing id, token-cost annotation, latency breakdown (queue, compute, network).

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Latency SLOs: median (p50) generation latency <= 120ms for short-turnbody (<=128 tokens) on Hosted small model profile; p95 <= 400ms. Dedicated SLO target: p95 <= 250ms.
- Availability: Hosted: 99.5% monthly uptime; Dedicated: 99.9% monthly uptime.
- Cost per token: Target economic envelope for Hosted API: $0.0008 - $0.0018 per token (model dependent) for common mid-sized models after batching/caching.
- Security: All customer data encrypted at rest and in transit; integrations with KMS for Private deployments.
- Compliance: Provide SOC2 controls and customer evidence package for Dedicated/Private.

Acceptance criteria (GA):
- End-to-end integration tests pass (>= 99.5% green) across 3 synthetic workload profiles (chat, embeddings, rerank).
- Performance benchmarks against reference harness: p50/p95 within 10% of target SLOs across regionally representative hardware.
- Pricing & billing flows validated end-to-end in staging for hosted usage billing and Dedicated reservation billing.

Design & architecture notes
-------------------------
High-level components:
- API Gateway (hosted) - handles auth, quotas, and request routing. Owner: eng-platform API team.
- Policy Router - routes to runtime variants (quantized/FP16/FP32) by policy. Owner: serving-runtime.
- Serving Runtime - GPU-optimized inference engine with KV cache, continuous batching, and optimized kernels. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Observability Pipeline - trace and metric aggregation with per-route dashboards. Owner: eng-platform observability.

API contract examples:
- /v1/generate POST body (JSON):
  {
    "model": "redwood-2-medium",
    "input": "Summarize the following...",
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "stream": false
  }
- Response headers: x-request-id, x-route, x-billed-tokens

Configuration table (example)
| Field | Description | Default | Notes |
| model_profile | runtime profile (small/medium/large) | medium | maps to kernel/quantization selection |
| batch_window_ms | max batching window | 20 | tuning knob to trade latency vs throughput |
| kv_cache_enabled | prefix caching | true | can be disabled per-route |

Roadmap & themes (Q3 2026 – Q2 2027)
------------------------------------
- Q3 2026 (completed): foundational runtime optimizations, basic API parity, initial pricing experiments.
- Q4 2026 (GA): Unified API GA, Dedicated reservation beta->GA, first enterprise Private pilot.
- Q1 2027: Expand model catalog, advanced routing policies (cost-aware bursts), enterprise adoption playbooks.
- Q2 2027: Workspace and fine-grained role controls, expanded compliance evidence for EU/UK data residency.

Milestones and dates:
1. Feature-complete API for GA: 2026-10-15
2. Dedicated capacity SLAs & billing integration: 2026-10-30
3. Private deployment pilot (customer A & B): 2026-11-20
4. GA marketing launch and pricing publication: 2026-11-30

Pricing & packaging notes
------------------------
Pricing principles:
- Align price with unit economics and provide clear volume discounts for high-throughput customers.
- Separate pricing for Hosted (usage-based) and Dedicated (commit + overage) and Private (enterprise license + support).

Suggested packaging tiers (initial):
1. Developer (Hosted, self-serve)
   - Usage billing only. No SLA. Limited quota: 100k tokens/month free trial.
2. Business (Hosted + optional Dedicated burst)
   - Usage billing + optional monthly commitment. Soft SLA: 99.5% uptime. Priority support.
3. Enterprise (Dedicated/Private)
   - Reserved capacity contract, 99.9% SLA, dedicated CSM, advanced compliance add-ons.

Pricing examples (illustrative)
- Hosted (on commonly used mid model): $0.0012 / input token, $0.0012 / output token (metered separately).
- Dedicated: monthly commit starting at $50k/mo for 1x small-GPU pool equivalent. Overage billed at committed unit rate * 1.5.
- Private: license + support: $150k annual platform fee + per-node support charge.

Billing & metering details
- Billed unit = billed_token where billed_token = input_tokens + output_tokens + system_tokens (per-request).
- Billing export: CSV and customer-facing billing UI + S3 billing snapshot for Dedicated.

Release notes (GA – 2026-11-30)
-----------------------------
Highlights:
- Unified API: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank with streaming and function-calling support.
- Dedicated reservations: SLA configuration, commit ledger, and quota enforcement.
- Observability: per-route latency histograms, token cost breakdown, and first-party dashboards.

Detailed changes:
- Serving runtime: kernel selector v1.3, 15–25% throughput improvement on 40k sequence workloads.
- Policy router: initial cost-aware fallback with capacity scoring.
- Billing: detailed billing export for Dedicated and hosted usage.

Known limitations & mitigations:
- Early Private deployments require manual network vetting (onprem-packaging doc). Mitigation: standard checklist and on-site validation during phase 1.
- Rare p95 latency spikes under bursty tail loads. Mitigation: conservative defaults for batch_window_ms and automatic fallback to smaller model variant under sustained tail.

Rollout plan & launch checklist
------------------------------
1. Staging validation (owner: eng-platform)\\   - Run 3 workload harnesses (chat, embeddings, rerank) for 7 days.\\   - Validate billing and metering exports.
2. Beta (closed customers) (owner: customer-success)\\   - Invite 5 pilot customers, monitor SLOs, and collect feedback for 4 weeks.
3. GA release (owner: product + eng-sre)\\   - Gradual rollout: 25% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours per region.\\   - Rollback criteria: a) sustained p95 > 1.5x SLO for 30+ minutes b) error rate increase > 2x baseline for 15+ minutes.

Operational SLOs & alerting
---------------------------
- Latency SLOs (global): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms (Hosted base); Dedicated p95 <= 250ms.
- Error budget: 0.5% monthly error budget for Hosted; Dedicated negotiated per contract.
- Alerts: P1 for SLO breach (pager), P2 for degraded metrics (email + slack).

Appendices
---------
A. Example CLI smoke test (curl)
curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-medium","input":"Give a one-paragraph summary of Redwood Inference","max_tokens":64}'

B. Troubleshooting checklist for pilot customers
- Network: verify ports 443 outbound to api.redwoodinference.ai and S3 endpoints.
- Keys: ensure API keys provisioned with required scopes.
- Observability: provide sample traces and request-ids when reporting issues.
